COLORS LESSON · COLORS & SHADES · AGES 2–5 YEARS

Light Blue — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches light blue — the first SHADE on the shelf: a color you can MAKE.

What is this?

Light blue is a shade of blue — the color of the kite, the raindrop, the helmet and the cloud on the card. It is blue plus white stirred together: the sky on a soft day, the deep blue gone pale.

What does it mean?

Here is the big idea of the shade section: light blue is not FOUND in the crayon flap alone — it is MADE. Blue paint plus white paint, stirred slow, becomes light blue every single time. A shade is a color with a recipe.

What does the child need to know?

The child needs to: say "light blue", name the recipe (blue + white), and spot light blue high in the world — sky, rain, clouds, things that fly.

Why this matters

This is the thinking step up from naming: at four and five, a child can hold TWO colors in mind and predict the mix. Predicting is what scientists do — the shade cards are the first lab.

What it teaches

Prediction (what will blue plus white make?), following a recipe in order, and sky-words: light blue connects color to weather talk — rain, clouds, kites.

Words to learn

light blueshademixrecipekiteraindrophelmetcloudpalesky

Say this to your child

“"Light blue! It is blue plus white — the sky on a soft day. The kite is light blue, the raindrop is light blue, the helmet is light blue, the cloud is light blue. Shall we MAKE some? Blue, plus white… stir… LIGHT BLUE!"”

Step by step

  1. Hold the BLUE card and this one side by side. Two blues! Ask: "what is different?" (one is darker, one is lighter — pale, soft, washed-out).
  2. Reveal the recipe: light blue is blue PLUS WHITE. Say it like a magic spell — "blue, plus white… LIGHT BLUE!"
  3. Square hunt: the kite flies, the raindrop falls, the helmet protects, the cloud floats — four light blues that all live UP or come DOWN from up. Sky family.
  4. Mix it for real: blue paint, white paint, one spoon, one pot — stir slow and watch light blue arrive. Predict first, stir second, shout third.
  5. Close with the helmet question: why do kites and helmets share a color? (Both go fast and need to be seen!) Light blue is the look-at-me-in-the-sky color.

Look closer at the picture

The raindrop and the cloud are the same color but different SHAPES — one drops, one floats. And the kite has a bow on its tail. Light blue is the card with weather on it.

Ask your child

"What two colors make light blue?" (blue and white) "Which light blue thing falls from the sky?" (raindrop) "Which one do we wear to be safe?" (helmet)

What your child can say or do

Your child might mix a whole pot of light blue and paint the sky, the table and both hands. Hands wash; the recipe sticks forever.

Out in the real world

Bike helmets come in every color but light blue is a classic — and real raindrops really do look light blue against the window. The mixing recipe is the same one paint factories use, just bigger.

Try it together

Raindrop, raindrop, CLOUD: a duck-duck-goose variant — tap heads saying "raindrop, raindrop…" and the CLOUD call means chase, arms out, floating fast. Weather words ride along free.

Understanding check

Ask: "what is the recipe for light blue?" (blue plus white) "Point at something light blue in the room." (the hunt works for shades too) "Is light blue light or dark?" (light — and now they hear the pun)

This lesson pairs with the Light Blue flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Colors & Shades.
